Q28065719.summary: This corner fragment of a sarcophagus front shows a veiled woman seated solemnly on a high-backed chair, holding a swaddled infant on her lap; a bearded man with a scroll leans on the chair behind her, another man appears at the corner, and two women stand at the right, one of whom seems to touch the child. It is one of the earliest sculpted images of the Virgin and Child, probably part of an Adoration of the Magi or a scene of the Nativity.
facts: The fragment was acquired by the Musée Saint-Raymond in 1986 from a private collection near Uzès (Gard).

Scholars have suggested that the woman touching the child is the midwife Salome of the apocryphal Protoevangelium of James, and that the missing right part may have shown the Magi or the first bath of the newborn.
It measures about 55 × 50 cm and comes from a continuous-frieze sarcophagus.
Q28065719.notes: Dating: POP gives 300–350, the Sathma corpus 325–350. The exact narrative scene is uncertain. Wikidata records 400.
Q28065719.original_title: Cuve de sarcophage de la Vierge à l'Enfant
